# relay-api configuration

Generated by docuconf from the configuration contract of `relay-api`, exported by `docuconf-go` `0.1.0` (go). Do not edit this file: change the app's declaration, export the contract again, then run `docuconf docs`.

`relay-api` reads 5 environment variables and 1 file. None is required, 3 only under a condition, and 1 is secret.

## Contents

**[Environment variables](#environment-variables)**

- [`APP_ENV`](#app_env): Deployment environment; selects config/{env}.yaml
- [`LOG_FORMAT`](#log_format): Log output format
- [`LOG_SCHEMA_URL`](#log_schema_url): JSON schema the structured logs follow (required when `LOG_FORMAT` is `json`)
- [`TLS_CLIENT_CA_SUBJECT`](#tls_client_ca_subject): Subject of the CA that signs client certificates (required when `TLS_ENABLED` is `true`)
- [`TLS_ENABLED`](#tls_enabled): Serve HTTPS instead of HTTP

**[Files](#files)**

- [`serving-tls`](#serving-tls): Certificate the relay serves HTTPS with (required when `TLS_ENABLED` is `true`, secret)

**Also:** [Profiles](#profiles) · [Sources](#sources) · [Boot errors](#boot-errors)

## Files

The platform mounts each file at its path; the app reads it there. With `DOCUCONF_FILE_ROOT=./dev`, the SDK reads every path under `./dev` instead, for local runs.

### `serving-tls`

Certificate the relay serves HTTPS with

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `tls` (TLS key pair) |
| Required | only when [`TLS_ENABLED`](#tls_enabled) is `true` |
| Secret | yes: never write its value in code, docs or a values file |
| Path | `/etc/relay/tls` |
| Contents | a directory holding `tls.crt` and `tls.key` (PEM), as a `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret lays them out |
| Reload | `restart`: the app reads the file at startup; a changed source needs a rollout |
| Sources | `secret` (the whole `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret, with no key), `certificate`, `csi`, `injected` (the injector writes the file at the path) |
| Boot errors | `file_missing`, `file_unreadable`, `file_malformed`, `certificate_invalid`, `key_mismatch` |

## Profiles

`APP_ENV` selects which of the app's profile files load: `production`. When it is unset, the profile is `development`. A profile's defaults apply only when it is selected, and the platform's values override them.

## Sources

Where the platform may get each input from, as named in the tables above. A secret comes only from a secret store or an injector.

- `literal`: a literal value in the platform's values file
- `configMapKeyRef`: a key of a ConfigMap (`configMapKeyRef`), checked at boot
- `fieldRef`: a pod field from the Downward API (`fieldRef`), such as `metadata.namespace`
- `injected`: supplied when the container starts by an injector (`injected`), such as Bank-Vaults, `op run` or the Vault Agent injector; checked at boot
- `secret`: a Kubernetes Secret (`secret`), one key per file
- `certificate`: a cert-manager Certificate (`certificate`)
- `csi`: the Secrets Store CSI driver (`csi`)

## Boot errors

At boot the SDK checks every input and reports all problems together, one line each, with one of these codes. Secret values never appear in the messages.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `missing_required` | A required input is not set, and has no default. | Set it through one of its allowed sources. |
| `invalid_type` | The value does not parse as the input's type in its wire format, or a secret still holds an unresolved injector reference (`vault:`, `op://`, `ref+`). | Write the value in the input's wire format. For an injected secret, make sure the injector runs. |
| `not_in_enum` | The value is not one of the allowed values. | Use one of the listed values, spelled exactly as listed. |
| `file_missing` | The file is not at its path. | Give the input a source, and check that it is mounted at the declared path (or that its path variable points at it). |
| `file_unreadable` | The file exists but cannot be read. | Check the mount, the file mode and the user the app runs as. |
| `file_malformed` | The file does not parse in its format, is a directory, is not UTF-8 text, or holds too few certificates. | Fix the content so it parses in the declared format. |
| `certificate_invalid` | A certificate does not parse, has expired or is not yet valid, uses a key algorithm that is not allowed, or does not chain to `ca.crt`. | Issue a valid certificate that meets the input's constraints. |
| `key_mismatch` | `tls.key` does not match the certificate in `tls.crt`. | Supply the key and certificate from the same issuance. |
